subject.title: Support Azure Foundry GPT Realtime Talk via gateway relay

question: Should OpenClaw ship a first-class Azure Foundry Talk relay now, and should the initial supported credential contract be API-key relay only or API key plus Microsoft Entra/managed identity?
rationale: This changes Talk’s public provider/configuration surface and its credential boundary. The correct durable contract cannot be inferred from existing partial backend bridge support alone.

options.title: Start with server-side API keys
options.body: Add the Azure GA Gateway relay using SecretRef-compatible API-key configuration, preserve existing direct OpenAI behavior, and design Entra support as a separate follow-up.

options.title: Design API key and Entra together
options.body: Approve both credential modes before implementation, accepting a larger surface and a longer proof requirement.

options.title: Defer until Azure capacity exists
options.body: Keep the request open without implementation until a maintained Azure Realtime deployment is available for end-to-end validation.

recommendation.title: Start with server-side API keys
recommendation.body: Add the Azure GA Gateway relay using SecretRef-compatible API-key configuration, preserve existing direct OpenAI behavior, and design Entra support as a separate follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged realtime bridge work and current OpenAI Talk transport ownership make this the strongest routing candidate for the transport and configuration decision.
